subject: Request: mid-cycle tier swap and addendum for additional capacity
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@veridian.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-09T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Mid-cycle capacity increase — guidance on pricing and co-term?

Hi Olga,

Quick question — our usage spiked this quarter and we need an additional 50% capacity on the inference pool for three months while a new model rollout stabilizes. We'd like to avoid signing a full-year commit immediately and prefer a short mid-cycle addendum that co-terms with our existing renewal on 2027-02-01.

Can you outline options for:
- A temporary top-up (3 months) with pro-rated billing;
- A co-term path that annualizes the additional capacity for a modest discount;
- Any paperwork / PO timing we should expect?

I copied David (engineering lead) for capacity details. Attachment: current_usage_report.csv (exported from our ops dashboard).

Thanks,
Marta
Marta Lopez
Head of Platform Engineering
Veridian Systems
From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@veridian.com>
Cc: David Hart <david.hart@veridian.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle capacity increase — guidance on pricing and co-term?

Hi Marta — thanks for the heads up and the usage report. I can get you two concrete options by EOD Friday after a quick internal consult.

High level:
- Option 1: 3-month temporary top-up billed pro-rata against current rates, with a one-time volume discount (we usually cap mid-cycle discounts at ~12% for ad-hoc adds).
- Option 2: Convert the incremental capacity to a co-term annualized commit (from today through 2027-02-01) for a deeper discount (typically 13–16%), billed pro-rata for the remainder of the term and then normalized at renewal.

I'll loop in Ben and Marcus for commercial and Lauren for billing mechanics so we can include an amendment draft and expected invoice timing.

Cheers,
Olga
Senior Account Manager
Redwood Inference
From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-10T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Veridian — mid-cycle addendum pricing ask

Team — forwarding Marta's request. Key facts from the usage file: baseline committed capacity billing ~$72k/month; incremental request ~+50% (est. $36k/month at list). They want either a 3-month top-up or an annualized co-term to 2027-02-01.

Proposals for discussion (first pass):
1) Temporary Top-up (3 months)
   - Discount: 12% off list for the incremental capacity
   - Billing: one pro-rated invoice for the 3-month period (charged upfront or net-30 per their preference)
   - Rationale: preserves flexibility for customer, limited revenue exposure for us

2) Co-term Annualize (ends 2027-02-01)
   - Discount: 15% off list on the incremental capacity (we should ask for a minimum renewal guarantee)
   - Billing: pro-rata for remainder of current term, then regular renewal cadence
   - Rationale: better unit economics and retention signal; requires minimal contractual addendum

Questions for Lauren: can we accept a 15% band for a mid-cycle annualize without finance signoff? Also propose adding a clause: if usage falls below 75% of the incremental commit during the addendum, we revert to list rates for any additional requests.

Ben/Marcus — any appetite to sweeten with a short-term credit rather than discount to preserve list price reference? Marcus, can you state expected ACV uplift if they pick Option 2?

Thanks,
Olga
From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-10T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Veridian — mid-cycle addendum pricing ask

Olga / team —

Finance inputs:
- We can authorize up to 14% discount on a mid-cycle addendum without executive approval if the deal is billed upfront or we have a PO with credit terms capped at net-30. 15% requires approval from Sales Ops Director.
- Preferred billing mechanics: pro-rate remainder of current term and invoice separately for the top-up. For a 3-month temporary top-up billed upfront, we can issue a credit memo if they later annualize.
- Recommend adding a usage floor clause as you suggested; helps protect MRR.

If they want a credit vs discount, a one-time usage credit equal to the dollar-value of a 12% discount is fine; keep the contract at list to preserve reference pricing.

Lauren Bishop
Head of Revenue Ops
Redwood Inference
From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@veridian.com>, David Hart <david.hart@veridian.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-12T08:44:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle capacity increase — guidance on pricing and co-term?

Marta / David — thanks for the patience. After internal alignment here are two clean options we can move forward with:

Option A — Short-term top-up (recommended if you prefer flexibility)
- Duration: 3 months (2026-11-15 to 2027-02-15)
- Pricing: incremental capacity billed at list with a one-time 12% credit applied to the incremental seat/compute charges
- Billing: Pro-rated invoice covering the 3-month window, due net-30. We can invoice on 2026-11-15.
- Contract: simple addendum (no renewal pledge).

Option B — Co-term annualize (recommended if you expect sustained higher usage)
- Duration: Annualized for the remainder of term, co-term to 2027-02-01
- Pricing: incremental capacity at 15% off list; requires a minimum renewal signal (e.g., commit to renew incremental volume or equivalent at renewal)
- Billing: Pro-rata for remainder of current term, then normal renewal cadence. 15% discount will require Sales Ops Director approval; we can fast-track if you provide a PO.

Attachments: amendment_draft_v1.pdf (amendment with both options and precise proration math).

Next steps: 1) Tell me which option you prefer; 2) if Option B, provide a PO and we’ll submit for the 15% approval; 3) if Option A, confirm billing preference (invoice upfront vs net-30).

I can get a DocuSign link for the selected path once you confirm.

Best,
Olga
Senior Account Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@veridian.com>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Hart <david.hart@veridian.com>
Date: 2026-11-13T15:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle capacity increase — guidance on pricing and co-term?

Hi Olga — appreciate the clear options. We’ll take Option A (3-month top-up with the 12% credit) to preserve runway while we finish the rollout. Please proceed with the pro-rated invoice on 2026-11-15.

One ask from legal: can you include a short clause in the amendment clarifying that the credit is limited to the incremental capacity charges and does not modify existing SOW terms? Also please send a draft PO and expected invoice number so procurement can route quickly.

If you can send the DocuSign and PO draft today, I’ll loop Procurement and Legal and aim to have PO by EOD Tuesday.

Thanks — Marta
